issues.body: Carried over from round 1 and not addressed (the file is byte-identical). With --coverdir, write_results uses _fullmodname(filename) (trace.py:262, joined at :271), which strips the longest matching sys.path prefix and replaces os.sep with '.'. For this repo's flat scripts/*.py that yields the bare name — trace sets sys.path[0] = os.path.dirname(progname) (trace.py:717) and _fullmodname prefers the longest prefix (trace.py:133-140), so even with REPO_ROOT also on sys.path the result is still 'foo' — hence the instruction is correct AS USED HERE. It stops being correct for a module reached inside a package: pkg/foo.py is written as <dir>/pkg.foo.cover, and an agent following the rule literally would look for foo.cover, find nothing, and — exactly against the intent of this paragraph — may conclude 'no uncovered lines'. (Note the stdlib's own -C help text at trace.py:632-634 documents this wrongly as <dir>/<package>/<module>.cover, so an author cross-checking against --help is misled twice.)
issues.fix_hint: Optionally note that with -C the filename is the module's full DOTTED name (<dir>/<pkg>.<module>.cover), and that a missing cover file must be treated as an instrument failure, never as zero uncovered lines.
issues.title: Unaddressed from round 1: with -C <dir> the cover filename is the DOTTED full module name, so '<dir>/<module>.cover' holds only for top-level modules

issues.body: New this round; verified against trace.py, not asserted from memory. The added step says to append a never-called function and 'confirm its executable line appears as >>>>>>'. For a function like `def _never(): \"\"\"doc\"\"\"; x = 2; return x`, the three line classes behave differently in write_results_file (trace.py:310-324): the `def _never():` line IS executed at module-definition time under trace, so it lands in lines_hit and prints a COUNT, not '>>>>>>'; the docstring line is excluded from lnotab by _find_strings (trace.py:350-371, 384) and prints as blank padding; only the BODY statement lines (x = 2 / return x) are in lnotab-but-unhit and carry '>>>>>>'. So an author who validates by checking 'its executable line' and picks the def line — the one line that names the function, and the natural thing to grep for — sees a hit count and would wrongly conclude the instrument is broken (or, worse, 'fix' the command until the def line is marked). This is a small imprecision, but the very sentence it attaches to cites #756, whose failure was exactly mis-attributing coverage inside a never-called function ('counted docstring lines as covered, scored a never-called function at 6.2 %'), so the precision is cheap and on-topic. Not blocking: it fails toward distrusting a working instrument, not toward trusting a broken one.
issues.fix_hint: Say 'its BODY line' rather than 'its executable line' — e.g. 'confirm the function's body line (not its `def` line, which executes at import) appears as >>>>>>'. Optionally add that docstring lines are never marked, since _find_strings excludes them from the executable-line table.
issues.title: Instrument-validation step: the appended function's `def` line IS executed, so 'confirm its executable line appears as >>>>>>' can read as a false negative

issues.body: Carried over from round 1 and not addressed. This diff establishes that a count-only report cannot show never-executed lines, yet several existing comments still record measurements taken that way: scripts/dashboard-gen.py:2944 ('Measured with `python3 -m trace --count` before this change: BOTH refusal lines...'), scripts/triage.py:1921 ('measured with `python3 -m trace --count'), and the aside at scripts/triage.py:2742. Those files are outside this diff so this cannot be a blocker (and is filed against AGENTS.md only because the schema requires an in-diff path), and the claims may still be true — a NONZERO count is evidence even without --missing, and the neighbouring citations at scripts/triage.py:2031, scripts/model-health.py:4335 and scripts/pat-validity.py:2036 already use `--count --missing` correctly. But the bare-`--count` ones read as endorsements of the instrument this rule now calls unable-to-fail: the #958 duplication shape applied to prose. Same for the canonical copy in sparq-org/sparq's AGENTS.md, which this file's own preamble (AGENTS.md:24-30) requires be mirrored in the same wave and which I cannot see from this checkout.
issues.fix_hint: Either re-measure those call sites with `--count --missing` and update the comment wording, or state in the PR body that the sparq-org/sparq canonical copy is mirrored in this wave (or why not), per the preamble at AGENTS.md:24-30.
issues.title: Unaddressed from round 1: in-repo comments still cite bare `trace --count` as a coverage measurement this rule now declares vacuous

verdict.summary:
Docs-only change to AGENTS.md pre-flight item 1. The diff is IDENTICAL to round 1 (branch carries one commit, e6bf3158b; AGENTS.md untouched since), so nothing was pushed in response to round 1 and both of its nits still stand.

Trust-plane lens: no script, workflow, policy or orchestration file is touched. I confirmed AGENTS.md is only ever CITED in prose comments (dispatch-secrets-guard.py, retriage.py, ci-latency-alert.py, readme-runbook-check.py, ...) and never parsed by any checker, so no self-test, route, label set, arm-side classifier or gate can be affected and no default-allow path is opened. The change strictly STRENGTHENS a previously vacuous instrument.

I re-derived every technical claim from /usr/lib/python3.11/trace.py rather than trusting round 1:
(a) '--count alone never writes >>>>>>' is exact: lnotab is {} unless show_missing (266-269) and '>>>>>> ' is emitted solely for `lineno in lnotab` (317-320); -m/--missing wires straight into that parameter (635-637, 737). A count-only report physically cannot contain the marker, so grepping it returns a vacuous zero.
(b) '-C also writes a cover file for every module touched, including stdlib' is exact: is_ignored_filename only skips '<...>' pseudo-files (180-184) and --ignore-dir defaults to [] (651), so the never-glob warning is load-bearing.
(c) The stale-cover-file warning is exact: write_results runs after the traced program's try/except SystemExit (728-737), so a self-test that sys.exit()s during path discovery still leaves a cover file measuring almost nothing.
(d) The command ordering parses correctly (progname + REMAINDER, 657-660), and '<dir>/<module>.cover' is right for this repo's flat scripts/ because _fullmodname takes the LONGEST matching sys.path prefix (125-147) with sys.path[0] = dirname(progname) (717).
